papers.title_zh: 可手术早期NSCLC中SABR较手术切除3年全因死亡率更高（模拟靶试验）
papers.title_en: Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy Versus Surgical Resection for Early-Stage Non-Small Lung Cancer: An Emulated Target Trial.
papers.authors: Kagenaar E, Lugo-Palacios DG, Aggarwal A, Hutchings A, O'Neill S, Rachet B, Edwards J, Faivre-Finn C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Health Services Research and Policy, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, London, UK.
papers.results: 主要终点3年全因死亡率：SABR 30.3%，手术 21.6%，校正后平均绝对风险差 8.8个百分点（95% CI, 1.4 to 16.2；P = .02）。次要终点肺癌特异性死亡率：SABR 20.6%，手术 14.5%，平均绝对风险差 6.1 pp（95% CI, -0.6 to 12.9；P = .07）。80岁以上亚组3年全因死亡率校正平均绝对风险差 4.3 pp（95% CI, -3.7 to 12.3；P = .62）。
papers.authors_conclusion: This emulated target trial found higher 3-year all-cause mortality after SABR versus surgery in early-stage NSCLC suitable for either modality, supporting that surgical resection should remain the preferred option. The findings support SABR as a curative-intent alternative, particularly for older people.
papers.ai_note: 主要终点（3年全因死亡）显示SABR更差，但作者结论后半段强调SABR作为治愈性替代方案、尤其对老年患者，依据的是未达统计学显著的80岁以上亚组（P = .62）和P = .07的肺癌特异性死亡，属以非显著次要/亚组结果对冲主要终点；肺癌特异性死亡与复发等次要终点的CI跨0，复发未报告任何数值。观察性模拟靶试验，残余适应证混杂与工具变量的具体构建、弱工具检验、平衡性诊断在摘要中均未报告，方法学细节信息不足；样本量与分组极度不均衡（约1:4.5）。

pico.p: 2015-2020年诊断的T1-2N0M0 NSCLC、18-79岁且Zubrod PS 0-2或80岁以上且PS 0-1、诊断后6个月内接受治疗者，共12,546例（SABR 2,299例；手术10,247例）
pico.ic: 立体定向消融放疗（SABR）对比手术切除（观察性治疗分配，经工具变量分析校正适应证混杂）

papers.reason: 为不可手术之外、实际可接受两种治疗的早期NSCLC患者提供SABR与手术的比较效果证据，直接影响临床对高龄或手术风险患者治疗方式的权衡，同时为后续RCT设计与目标试验模拟方法学提供对照基线。
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) is standard of care for inoperable early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but there is little evidence to support SABR as an alternative to surgical resection. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have failed to recruit, and ongoing RCTs apply strict inclusion criteria. To our knowledge, this is the first emulated target trial comparing the effectiveness of SABR versus surgery in individuals with early-stage NSCLC eligible for either treatment. METHODS: We used England's National Cancer Registry data to identify individuals diagnosed with T1-2N0M0 NSCLC during 2015-2020, age 18-79 years with Zubrod performance status 0-2, or age 80+ years with performance status 0-1, who underwent SABR or surgical resection within 6 months of diagnosis. Treatment receipt was identified via linkage to Hospital Episode Statistics and the National Radiotherapy Data Set. The primary outcome was 3-year all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included lung cancer-specific mortality and recurrence. An instrumental variable analysis reduced the risk of confounding by indication. RESULTS: A total of 12,546 met the eligibility criteria (2,299 SABR; 10,247 surgery). After adjustment, 3-year all-cause mortality estimates were 30.3% (SABR) and 21.6% (surgery; mean absolute risk difference 8.8 percentage points [pp], [95% CI, 1.4 to 16.2]; P = .02). Lung cancer-specific mortality estimates were 20.6% (SABR) and 14.5% (surgery; mean absolute risk difference 6.1 pp [95% CI, -0.6 to 12.9]; P = .07). The adjusted mean absolute risk difference in 3-year all-cause mortality for those age 80+ years was 4.3 pp ([95% CI, -3.7 to 12.3]; P = .62). CONCLUSION: This emulated target trial found higher 3-year all-cause mortality after SABR versus surgery in early-stage NSCLC suitable for either modality, supporting that surgical resection should remain the preferred option. The findings support SABR as a curative-intent alternative, particularly for older people.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Salvage esophagectomy is considered the standard curative treatment for localized residual or recurrent esophageal cancer after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), but it is associated with substantial morbidity. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as a less invasive alternative. We compared the outcomes of salvage esophagectomy and PDT for localized residual or recurrent esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) after definitive CRT or radiotherapy (RT). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 91 patients with cT1-2N0M0 residual or recurrent ESCC after definitive CRT or RT who underwent salvage esophagectomy (n = 33) or PDT (n = 58) at a single institution. Overall survival (OS), disease-specific survival (DSS), and treatment-related outcomes were evaluated. RESULTS: Patients treated with PDT were significantly older and had a higher comorbidity burden than those undergoing salvage esophagectomy. Salvage esophagectomy achieved an R0 resection rate of 94.0% but was associated with severe postoperative complications in 48.5% of patients, including one treatment-related death. In the PDT group, initial local complete response was achieved in 74.1% of patients, with one grade 3 adverse event and no treatment-related mortality. No significant differences were observed between the groups in OS (p = 0.597) or DSS (p = 0.670). CONCLUSIONS: This study does not establish equivalence or non-inferiority between PDT and salvage esophagectomy. PDT demonstrated a favorable safety profile and may offer an organ-preserving salvage treatment option for carefully selected patients with localized residual or recurrent ESCC after definitive CRT or RT, particularly those unsuitable for surgery because of advanced age, substantial comorbidities, or limited surgical tolerance.

papers.title_en: Protein Biomarkers of Lung Cancer Risk Among Individuals Who Never Smoked.
papers.authors: Zahed H, Bulos-Salim C, Alcala K, AlWaheidi S, Feng X, Wang Y, Patel AV, Le Marchand L et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: International Agency for Research on Cancer/World Health Organization (IARC/WHO), Lyon, France.
papers.results: LC3中以FDR校正P<.05为阈值，2种蛋白与不吸烟者肺癌相关：CEACAM5（OR, 1.65 [95% CI, 1.31-2.09]）和CEACAM6（OR, 1.72 [95% CI, 1.33-2.22]）。UK Biobank中两者的关联在按吸烟史不分组、随访5年的参与者中得到重复验证（CEACAM5: HR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.66-2.22]；CEACAM6: HR, 1.86 [95% CI, 1.59-2.16]）。CEACAM5与CEACAM6相关性较弱（LC3中Pearson ρ = 0.25），相互校正后两者仍保持高相对风险关联。既往已确认的36种吸烟相关肺癌蛋白标志物中，多数在不吸烟者中无关联证据（吸烟相关 vs 非吸烟相关肺癌的中位OR分别为 1.47 [IQR, 1.38-1.61] vs 1.01 [IQR, 0.94-1.13]）。
papers.authors_conclusion: In this nested case-control study, 2 proteins were identified, CEACAM5 and CEACAM6, that were associated with lung cancer in PWNS. Larger studies are needed to evaluate whether there are additional biomarkers associated with lung cancer in PWNS and whether they can identify PWNS with high lung cancer risk.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Approximately one-quarter of lung cancers occur in people who never smoked (PWNS). For smoking-associated lung cancer, blood-based protein biomarkers can improve risk assessment. OBJECTIVE: To identify protein biomarkers for lung cancer among PWNS. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nested case-control study from 4 cohorts in the Lung Cancer Cohort Consortium (LC3) was conducted for discovery to identify proteins, and a cohort study was conducted using data in the UK Biobank for replication. Participants were from the US, China, and the United Kingdom and donated blood samples between 1996 and 2010. Lung cancer case-control pairs of PWNS from 4 cohorts in the LC3 were matched by cohort, age, sex, and blood collection date. In addition, 49 291 participants in the UK Biobank were included. Data were analyzed from March 2024 to May 2025. EXPOSURE: A total of 2821 circulating proteins measured in prediagnostic blood samples collected up to 5 years before lung cancer diagnosis for cases. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary measures were odds ratios (ORs) for discovery and hazard ratios (HRs) for replication. RESULTS: Among 180 case-control pairs of PWNS (360 participants) in the 4 LC3 cohorts, 256 participants (71.1%) were female, and the median (IQR) age at enrollment was 66 (55-70) years. In LC3, using a false discovery rate-adjusted P value threshold of .05, 2 proteins were identified as being associated with lung cancer among PWNS: carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule 5 (CEACAM5) (OR, 1.65 [95% CI, 1.31-2.09]) and CEACAM6 (OR, 1.72 [95% CI, 1.33-2.22]). Associations for both proteins were successfully replicated among participants analyzed regardless of smoking history across 5 years of follow-up in the UK Biobank (CEACAM5: HR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.66-2.22]; CEACAM6: HR, 1.86 [95% CI,1.59-2.16]). The correlation between CEACAM5 and CEACAM6 was weak (Pearson ρ = 0.25 in the LC3); therefore, both proteins maintained associations with high relative risks after mutual adjustment. For 36 proteins previously identified as robust markers of smoking-related lung cancer, most showed no evidence of an association among PWNS (median OR, 1.47 [IQR, 1.38-1.61] vs 1.01 [IQR, 0.94-1.13] in smoking-related vs nonsmoking lung cancer). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this nested case-control study, 2 proteins were identified, CEACAM5 and CEACAM6, that were associated with lung cancer in PWNS. Larger studies are needed to evaluate whether there are additional biomarkers associated with lung cancer in PWNS and whether they can identify PWNS with high lung cancer risk.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplant is associated with increased mortality. Whether PGD increases mortality via long-term effects on allograft function is poorly understood. OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the association of PGD with potential lung function and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD). METHODS: We included lung transplant recipients enrolled in an 8-center prospective cohort study from 2007-2018. PGD was defined by ISHLT criteria. Linear mixed effects and logistic regression models evaluated the association between PGD and maximum potential forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) and whether Global Lung Function Initiative defined (GLI) predicted FEV1 was attained, respectively. Flexible parametric survival models evaluated the association between PGD and CLAD, accounting for confounding and mortality as a competing risk. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 2419 recipients, 510 had PGD. Recipients with PGD had lower maximum potential FEV1 (-311 ml, 95% CI -245 to -377 ml) and were less likely to achieve GLI-predicted FEV1 (probability difference -12.5%, 95% CI -17 to -8%). 930 recipients developed CLAD (405 obstructive, 525 restrictive) over median (IQR) 5.9 (3.0-8.0 years). The 5-year cumulative incidence of CLAD did not differ by PGD (cumulative difference: -2.2%, 95% CI - 6.4% to 1.9%). This association was not modified by age, sex, BMI, pretransplant diagnosis, or transplant type. PGD was not associated with a difference in cumulative incidence of obstructive or restrictive CLAD (cumulative difference -1.2% and -0.8%, respectively). CONCLUSION: PGD is associated with reduced lung function and lower likelihood of achieving GLI-predicted maximum potential lung function but not CLAD.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Type 2 inflammation is present in 20%-40% of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). OBJECTIVE: To perform in-depth analyses of the efficacy of dupilumab on lung function parameters in patients with COPD and type 2 inflammation. METHODS: In BOREAS (NCT03930732) and NOTUS (NCT04456673), patients with COPD and type 2 inflammation were randomized to dupilumab 300 mg (n = 938) or placebo (n = 936) subcutaneously every 2 weeks for 52 weeks. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Dupilumab versus placebo improved pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1; least squares mean difference: 83 [95% confidence interval (CI): 53-112] mL; P < .0001), post-bronchodilator FEV1 (71 [41-101] mL; P < .0001), pre-bronchodilator forced vital capacity (FVC; 64 [26-102] mL; P = .0009), post-bronchodilator FVC (41 [3-79] mL; P = .0341), post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC (0.016 [0.010-0.022]; P < .0001), and forced expiratory flow 25%-75% of FVC (78 [45-111] mL/s; P < .0001) at week 12 and sustained to week 52. Improvements in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 were observed regardless of smoking status or the presence of co-existing emphysema; greater improvements were observed in patients with higher baseline eosinophil counts or fractional exhaled nitric oxide. Dupilumab versus placebo achieved >100 mL improvements in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at week 12 (42.2% vs 31.1%) and week 52 (36.9% vs 31.2%), with a similar proportion for post-bronchodilator FEV1 at weeks 12 and 52. CONCLUSIONS: Dupilumab treatment resulted in early and sustained improvements across multiple spirometric lung function parameters in patients with COPD and type 2 inflammation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neurogenic dysphagia frequently constitutes a major barrier to decannulation for tracheostomized patients. Conventional nasogastric tube (NGT) feeding may promote disuse atrophy of swallowing musculature and persistent aspiration risk. Intermittent oro-esophageal tube (IOE) feeding, a physiologically oriented modality mimicking natural swallowing, may accelerate decannulation, yet high-quality evidence is lacking. METHODS: In this multicenter randomized controlled trial conducted at three tertiary academic centers in China, tracheostomized adults with neurogenic dysphagia were randomly assigned 1:1 to IOE or NGT. All participants received standardized pharmacological treatment, pulmonary rehabilitation, and structured swallowing training, and entered an institutional decannulation protocol with predefined readiness criteria. The primary outcome was time from protocol entry to actual decannulation. Secondary outcomes included the 30-day successful decannulation rate, nutritional indices, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life. Outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to allocation. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. RESULTS: A total of 140 patients were randomized to IOE (n = 70) or NGT (n = 70). Time to decannulation was shorter with IOE (22.16 ± 1.86 vs. 26.33 ± 1.30 days; between-group difference, 4.17 days; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.90-6.44; p < 0.001; log-rank p = 0.005). The 30-day successful decannulation rate was higher with IOE (65.71% vs. 47.14%; absolute difference, 18.57% points; 95% CI, 2.43-34.71; p = 0.028). At 1 month, the IOE group demonstrated greater improvements in body mass index, serum albumin, serum prealbumin, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life (all p < 0.001). Pharyngeal discomfort was less frequent with IOE (14.06% vs. 34.21%; p = 0.006); no Grade Ⅲ or higher adverse events occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Intermittent oro-esophageal tube feeding shortens time to decannulation and improves nutritional, swallowing, and quality-of-life outcomes compared with nasogastric tube feeding in tracheostomized patients with neurogenic dysphagia. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06791590, registration date January 19, 2025.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) integrated with mobile cone-beam CT (mCBCT) has emerged as a promising platform for the diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs), with high diagnostic yield and low complication rates. However, no data have been reported in a Korean population. We evaluated the diagnostic yield and safety of ssRAB integrated with mCBCT in a Korean cohort. METHODS: This prospective, single-center cohort (the ULSAN-ION study) enrolled patients undergoing ssRAB with integrated mCBCT from July 2025 to April 2026 (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07057648). Diagnostic yield was assessed using the strict ATS/ACCP definition at the per-nodule and per-patient levels. RESULTS: A total of 111 patients with 140 PPNs were enrolled. Median age was 64.0 years (IQR, 55.5-69.5), and 51.4 % were male. Median nodule size was 14.0 mm (IQR, 10.0-19.2), and nodule morphology included solid (57.9 %), part-solid (28.6 %), and pure ground-glass opacity (13.6 %). A CT bronchus sign was absent in 70.7 % of nodules. mCBCT was performed in 88.6 % of nodules, with tool-in-lesion confirmation in 77.9 % and an overall tool-to-lesion rate of 99.1 %. Per-nodule diagnostic yield was 85.0 % (119/140) and per-patient diagnostic yield was 90.1 % (100/111). A malignant diagnosis was established in 75.7 % of patients, most commonly adenocarcinoma, and a specific benign diagnosis in 14.4 %. Pneumothorax occurred in 4.5 % of patients, with chest tube insertion required in 2.7 %. Airway bleeding (Nashville Grade ≥ 2) occurred in 1.8 %, with no Grade ≥ 3 events. CONCLUSION: This first prospective Korean experience demonstrates that ssRAB integrated with mCBCT achieves high diagnostic yield with an acceptable safety profile for PPN diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The role of local ablative therapy (LAT) in patients with locally advanced NSCLC who develop oligoprogressive disease (oligo-PD) after chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and maintenance durvalumab remains unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included patients with locally advanced NSCLC who developed oligo-PD after CRT and at least one dose of durvalumab and received exclusive LAT at seven centers (2016-2023). Oligo-PD was defined as ≤ 5 progressive sites across ≤ 3 organs. LAT comprised surgery, radical-dose radiotherapy, or cryoablation with curative intent to all progression sites. PFS and OS were measured from LAT using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox models assessed prognostic factors. RESULTS: Among 198 patients with progression during or after durvalumab, 41 received exclusive LAT for oligo-PD. LAT consisted of radiotherapy, surgery ± radiotherapy, and cryoablation in 71%, 27%, and 2%, respectively. Median PFS was 11.0 months (95% CI 7.9-36.7) and median OS was 18.7 months (95% CI 11.1-NR). One- and two-year PFS rates were 47.2% and 32.6%; corresponding OS rates were 61.7% and 46.1%. In multivariable analyses, PFS ≥ 12 months from durvalumab initiation (OS: HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.12-0.86; p = 0.023; PFS: HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.17-0.87; p = 0.022) and absence of brain metastases (OS: HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.11-0.87; p = 0.026; PFS: HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.19-0.99; p = 0.049) were associated with better outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with oligo-PD after CRT and durvalumab, exclusive LAT may be feasible and associated with encouraging survival. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

papers.title_zh: 年龄加权红细胞分布宽度指数（AWRI）预测ICU急性呼吸衰竭患者院内死亡：24,709例回顾性队列研究
papers.title_en: Age-weighted red cell distribution width index for predicting mortality in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Lin Z, Chen S, Zhan R, Deng J, Liu P, Li Z, Mo J, He J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Guangdong Medical University, Zhanjiang, Guangdong, 524000, China.
papers.results: 院内死亡率18.8%。全调整模型中AWRI与死亡独立相关（Q4 vs Q1：HR 1.42，95%CI 1.28-1.59，P<0.001）。限制性立方样条显示显著非线性关系及两个阈值：AWRI≤16.3%与显著降低的死亡风险相关（HR 0.453，95%CI 0.281-0.730），AWRI≥27%与持续升高的风险相关（HR 1.31，95%CI 1.22-1.40）。机器学习分析中AWRI为17项入院常规变量中重要性最高的预测因子（mean |SHAP| = 0.30），XGBoost模型AUC 0.748，优于APACHE IV（AUC 0.670，P<0.001）。AWRI判别力优于常规RDW（AUC 0.608 vs 0.572，P<0.001）。
papers.authors_conclusion: AWRI独立预测ICU急性呼吸衰竭患者的院内死亡，在判别能力上优于常规RDW和APACHE IV，且从单次常规血常规检查获得与SOFA-2相当的性能；其临床可解释的非线性风险阈值与最高的机器学习重要性支持将其整合入ICU入院常规风险分层。
papers.ai_note: AUC 0.748为含AWRI在内的17变量XGBoost整合模型的性能，并非AWRI单项指标性能；AWRI单独判别力仅AUC 0.608，属中低水平，摘要将两者并列叙述易被误读为AWRI本身达到0.748。结论声称与SOFA-2性能相当，但摘要未报告任何SOFA-2的AUC或比较统计量，信息不足。仅单中心数据库回顾性数据，摘要未提及外部验证、校准度或决策曲线，亦未报告与SOFA/APACHE以外评分的完整比较；无前瞻性验证。信息不足处：样条阈值HR的参照组定义、Q1-Q3各组数值、区分度之外的重分类指标。

pico.p: eICU数据库中经顺序排除后纳入的24,709例ICU急性呼吸衰竭患者（中位年龄66.0岁，男性54.0%），院内死亡率18.8%
pico.ic: 按AWRI四分位分组（Q4 vs Q1）及非线性阈值分层比较；与常规RDW、APACHE IV及17项入院常规变量的机器学习模型比较，无干预性对照

papers.reason: 为ICU急性呼吸衰竭患者入院时简易风险分层工具的选择提供证据（AWRI可由血常规+年龄直接计算），并展示以年龄校正RDW改进传统炎症/预后标志物的方法学路径；对非肿瘤性危重症呼吸患者的预后沟通与资源分配决策有参考价值。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory failure (ARF) represents one of the most common critical illnesses in intensive care units (ICUs), with persistently high mortality rates. Red cell distribution width (RDW) has demonstrated value in predicting prognosis of respiratory diseases; however, conventional RDW fails to account for age-related effects on red blood cell morphology. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the Age-Weighted RDW Index (AWRI) in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized data from the eICU Collaborative Research Database, enrolling 24,709 ICU patients with acute respiratory failure after sequential exclusion. AWRI was defined as RDW × (1 + age/100). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and five machine learning algorithms with SHAP-based interpretability were applied to evaluate the independent prognostic value and nonlinear risk patterns of AWRI. RESULTS: Among 24,709 patients (median age 66.0 years; 54.0% male), in-hospital mortality was 18.8%. AWRI was independently associated with mortality in the fully adjusted model (Q4 vs. Q1: HR 1.42, 95% CI 1.28-1.59, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis identified a significant nonlinear relationship with two key thresholds: AWRI ≤ 16.3% was associated with markedly reduced mortality risk (HR 0.453, 95% CI 0.281-0.730) and AWRI ≥ 27% with persistently elevated risk (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.22-1.40). In machine learning analysis, AWRI ranked as the highest-importance predictor among 17 routine admission variables (mean |SHAP| = 0.30), and the XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.748, outperforming APACHE IV (AUC = 0.670, P < 0.001). AWRI demonstrated superior discrimination compared with conventional RDW (AUC 0.608 vs. 0.572, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: AWRI independently predicts in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure, outperforming both conventional RDW and APACHE IV in discriminative ability and achieving comparable performance to SOFA-2 from a single routine blood count. Its clinically interpretable nonlinear risk thresholds and highest-ranked machine learning importance support integration into routine risk stratification at ICU admission.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: High flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) has become a common first-line practice for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (ARF). In immunocompromised patients, ARF is the leading cause of ICU admission, yet a randomized trial found no overall benefit of HFNO in this population. OBJECTIVES: To assess whether baseline characteristics influence HFNO's effectiveness in preventing invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in immunocompromised patients with ARF. METHODS: A causal forest machine-learning algorithm was derived in the HIGH trial (776 patients randomized to HFNO or conventional oxygen) to predict the HFNO effects on day-28 IMV incidence. Patients with a "do-not-intubate" order (n = 72) were excluded. Model performance was validated through 500 bootstrap iterations and patients were categorized into terciles based on predicted HFNO benefit. Transportability of the model was assessed in an independent observational cohort (818 patients). MAIN RESULTS: Among the 704 participants, HFNO's average effect on day-28 IMV was not significant. However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment responses was identified (predicted benefit: from 20.2% [IQR 15.5%-23.9%] absolute IMV risk reduction with HFNO to 7.4% risk reduction [2.9%-11.2%] with conventional oxygen). Patients with the highest predicted benefit were older, more frequently solid organ transplant recipients, less neutropenic, more severely hypoxemic/tachycardic, but with lower non-respiratory sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores. In this subgroup, HFNO was associated with a significant lower incidence of IMV. In the observational cohort, the benefit-ranking performance was preserved, although absolute effect estimates were less calibrated. CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest HFNO might benefit specific immunocompromised patients with ARF. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Concurrently measured PaO2/FIO2 (PF) and SpO2/FIO2 (SF) exhibit moderate-to-high correlation. However, their performance for risk stratification when using PF if available, or SF if not, as operationalized in recent acute respiratory distress (ARDS) and sequential organ failure assessment score (SOFA-2) guidance, is unknown. OBJECTIVES: Measure the prognostic performance of PF- and SF-defined hypoxemic respiratory failure severity. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients receiving invasive or non-invasive mechanical ventilation, or high-flow nasal oxygen across 58 Common Longitudinal ICU data Format (CLIF) consortium hospitals. We used the lowest PF, if available, or SF if not, from the first 24 hours of respiratory support to define ARDS and SOFA-2 severity categories. We characterized risk of in-hospital death or hospice discharge by day 28 by severity category, and evaluated prognostic performance using logistic regression models with area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROC). We then evaluated whether PF- or SF-defined patients' risk of death or hospice differed after adjustment for other patient risk factors. RESULTS: Oxygenation severity was defined with PF in n = 40,820 patients, and SF in n = 16,906. In-hospital death or hospice discharge was higher for PF (33.4%) versus SF (23.4%) patients, overall, and within each severity category. The SF-AUROC was numerically higher (0.60 [95%-CI:0.58-0.61]) than PF-AUROC (0.57 [95%-CI:0.57-0.58]). After adjustment, there was no statistical difference in outcome between PF and SF-defined patients. CONCLUSIONS: PF and SF thresholds for severity categories recommended as equivalent in ARDS and SOFA-2 guidance define populations with different mortality, but have similar risk discrimination.

papers.abstract_en: In recent years, significant progress has been made in developing targeted therapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, these therapies are only applicable to specific NSCLC groups with corresponding gene mutations. Therefore, developing novel targeted therapies to benefit more patients remains an important task. Our prior work demonstrated that LKB1-mutant NSCLC cells are highly susceptible to cell death induced by glucose starvation. In this study, we investigated a novel combinational therapeutic strategy utilizing a sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor canagliflozin and a covalent KRASG12C inhibitor adagrasib, two clinically approved therapeutics, to selectively target LKB1-KRASG12C co-mutated NSCLC. First, we verified the co-occurrence of LKB1 and KRAS mutations in clinical NSCLC cohorts. Second, compared to other SGLT2 inhibitors, canagliflozin induced higher cytotoxicity in LKB1-mutant cells, and SGLT2 knockdown partially attenuated this effect. Mechanistically, the high susceptibility to canagliflozin was associated with impaired activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Furthermore, canagliflozin suppressed mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) activity and robustly inhibited cell growth in LKB1-mutant models in vitro. Third, adagrasib exhibited selective cytotoxicity in KRASG12C-mutated NSCLC. Finally, the combination of canagliflozin and adagrasib synergistically reduced cell viability in LKB1-KRASG12C co-mutated H23 and H2122 cells in vitro. Importantly, canagliflozin attenuated the adaptive MAPK signaling rebound induced by adagrasib in vitro. The therapeutic potential of this combination was confirmed in an H2122 nude mouse xenograft model in vivo. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that a combination of canagliflozin and adagrasib suppresses LKB1-KRASG12C co-mutated NSCLC, laying a solid preclinical foundation for developing a new therapeutic strategy for this group of NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) arise from heterogeneous inflammatory and infectious processes, yet systemic corticosteroids and antibiotics are often prescribed empirically. This narrative review evaluates biomarkers according to the acute treatment decisions they can support, drawing on randomized trials and supporting clinical studies evaluated through August 9, 2026. Blood eosinophils have the most developed evidence for corticosteroid guidance: trials support treatment selection or withholding in primary care and serial treatment shortening after an initial dose in hospitalized patients. C-reactive protein supports antibiotic stewardship most clearly in primary care, with more limited inpatient evidence. Procalcitonin can reduce antibiotic use in selected non-intensive-care inpatients, whereas the intensive-care trial failed to establish non-inferiority for mortality and did not reduce antibiotic exposure. These findings depend on the tested population, sampling time, threshold, and treatment rule. Rapid molecular pathogen tests improve diagnostic yield and turnaround time; their integration into COPD-specific treatment algorithms remains a research priority. Multimarker strategies and acute biologic treatment offer further avenues for investigation, with acute biologic evidence currently derived from a mixed asthma/COPD population. Organizing evidence around a biomarker-decision-population framework separates established stewardship applications from emerging treatment strategies. Clinical utility ultimately depends on whether the complete strategy preserves or improves patient outcomes and can be delivered reliably in routine care.

papers.abstract_en: A significant challenge for improving the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy is the concurrent activation of Tregs, which can dampen antitumor responses. Thus, elucidating the mechanisms that maintain Treg-suppressive function within the tumor microenvironment is critical. Here, we identified an accumulation of N-acetyltransferase 10-modified (NAT10-modified) RNA, particularly in NAT10+FOXP3+ Tregs, in human non-small cell lung cancer. Genetic ablation of Nat10 in tumor-infiltrating (TI) Tregs, or pharmacological inhibition of NAT10 expression, significantly reduced the PD-1+ Treg/CD8+ T cell ratio. These effects were accompanied by an increase in IFN-γ+ Tregs, a reduction in the immunosuppressive activity of Tregs, and inhibition of tumor progression. Mechanistically, NAT10 promotes TI Treg infiltration and activation independently of its RNA-modifying function by directly interacting with FOXP3 and chromatin, modulating local 3D chromatin contacts. Combined administration of anti-PD-1 antibodies and a NAT10 inhibitor further impaired TI Treg-mediated immunosuppression, leading to enhanced tumor control. Our findings demonstrate that NAT10 is a key regulator of TI Treg fragility and function and that its inhibition may enhance the therapeutic efficacy of ICB.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Aberrant glycolysis and lactate accumulation are hallmarks of solid tumors, yet how tumor-derived lactate contributes to tumor progression has not been fully defined. This study intends to examine the role of glycolysis in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) growth and immunosuppression, and to explore the underpinning mechanisms. METHODS: Syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma models and autochthonous KrasLSL-G12D LUAD mice were used. Glycolysis was inhibited by 2-DG or LDH knockdown, followed by tumor growth and immune-cell composition assessments. Therapeutic anti-IL-35 blockade and CD8+ T depletion were performed using neutralizing antibodies. Chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1) expression, regulatory B cell (Breg) polarization, and B-cell-mediated T-cell suppression were assessed by flow cytometry, RNA sequencing, qPCR, ELISA, immunohistochemistry, and co-culture assays. CUT&Tag, chromatin immunoprecipitation, co-immunoprecipitation, and cell-free transferase assays were used to define the lactylation mechanism. RESULTS: Glycolysis restriction suppressed tumor growth and metastatic colonization, reduced CD1dhiCD5+IL-35+ Bregs, and restored GZMB+CD8+ T cells. CHI3L1 was markedly downregulated after glycolysis inhibition, whereas recombinant CHI3L1 restored IL-13Rα2+ Breg polarization and impaired CD8+ T-cell responses through STAT3 activation. Lactate increased H3K9 lactylation and CHI3L1 expression, while glycolysis inhibition reduced H3K9la enrichment at the Chi3l1 promoter. HBO1 directly catalyzed H3K9 lactylation and promoted CHI3L1 production. Genetic or pharmacological HBO1 blockade reduced Bregs, enhanced cytotoxic T-cell activity, and improved the efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the participation of an HBO1-H3K9la-CHI3L1–IL-13Rα2-STAT3 axis in tumor glycolysis-established Breg polarization and CD8+ T dysfunction. Targeting HBO1 may provide a strategy to enhance the efficacy of PD-1 blockade in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Long-acting drug-Fc conjugate (CD388) has emerged as a new class of antivirals against influenza A and B, yet the mechanisms governing how Fc conjugation reshapes small-molecule function remain undefined. Here we establish a programmable multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform by click chemistry that enables flexible combination of valencies and conjugated drugs, allowing systematic interrogation of valency-dependent antiviral mechanisms. Using zanamivir as a model, mono-, di-, and trivalent zanamivir are conjugated with Fc, with trivalent zanamivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-Z3) exhibiting higher activity than lower-valent AVCs. AVC-Z3 induces inter-virion aggregation, thereby coupling blockade of viral entry with restriction of viral release. This cross-linking-mediated dual-stage inhibition represents a mechanistic shift from neuraminidase suppression to physical viral immobilization. Furthermore, trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate (AVC-P3) is synthesised and exhibits stronger antiviral activity than AVC-Z3 in vitro, with much longer half-life in vivo than AVC-Z3, and CD388 with YTE mutation. The in vivo antivirus efficacy of AVC-P3 surpasses other AVCs, baloxavir, and CD388 in H1N1-, H3N2-, H5N1-, and influenza B-infection mice models. Together, our findings define ligand valency as a determinant of antiviral mechanism.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) is vital for diagnosing mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy. This study investigated the diagnostic performance of Hounsfield unit (HU) values and PET-CT SUVmax in differentiating malignant from benign lymph nodes. METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 168 patients who underwent EBUS-TBNA between 2021 and 2024. Data on demographics, smoking history, HU, PET-CT SUVmax, and EBUS lymph node measurements were collected. Statistical methods included logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis to assess diagnostic accuracy. RESULTS: Malignant lymph nodes had significantly lower HU values and larger EBUS dimensions (p < 0.05). The PET‒CT SUVmax did not significantly differ (p = 0.607). ROC analysis revealed that HU had the highest predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.678). Logistic regression identified HU as an independent predictor of malignancy. CONCLUSION: CT-based HU measurements have greater diagnostic value than PET-CT SUVmax in predicting malignancy in EBUS-TBNA-biopsied lymph nodes. HU could aid in guiding biopsy decisions and improve diagnostic accuracy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, necessitating the identification of novel molecular mechanisms and therapeutic targets. GATA5, a member of the GATA family of transcription factors, has been implicated as a potential tumor suppressor in various malignancies; however, its role and regulatory mechanisms in NSCLC pathogenesis remain largely unexplored. METHODS: GATA5 expression and promoter methylation status were assessed in NSCLC cell lines, patient tissues, and public databases using RT-PCR, western blot, methylation-specific PCR, and immunohistochemistry. Functional studies were performed using in vitro assays (proliferation, colony formation, apoptosis, migration, invasion) and in vivo xenograft models. Mechanistic insights were obtained through RNA sequencing, chromatin immunoprecipitation, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and rescue experiments. The therapeutic potential of CNR1 inhibition was evaluated using the selective antagonist AM251 alone and in combination with cisplatin. RESULTS: GATA5 was frequently silenced by promoter hypermethylation in NSCLC, and low GATA5 expression correlated with poor patient prognosis. Functionally, GATA5 acted as a potent tumor suppressor, inhibiting proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth while promoting apoptosis. Mechanistically, GATA5 directly bound to the SDPR promoter to activate its transcription, and SDPR was identified as a critical mediator of GATA5's tumor-suppressive effects. The GATA5-SDPR axis negatively regulated CNR1, an oncogenic effector. Pharmacological inhibition of CNR1 with AM251 reversed the pro-tumorigenic effects of GATA5 loss and synergized with cisplatin to enhance anti-tumor efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings establish the GATA5-SDPR-CNR1 axis as a critical tumor-suppressive pathway in NSCLC. Targeting CNR1 represents a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome cisplatin resistance and improve outcomes in patients with GATA5-silenced tumors.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic progressive interstitial lung disease with a high mortality rate. Reliable biomarker can enable clinicians to judge the development and prognosis of IPF.ObjectivesThis study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) for predicting all-cause mortality in IPF.DesignThis retrospective cohort study enrolled patients hospitalized with IPF between January 1st, 2015 and May 31st, 2023.MethodsData was collected regarding patient demographics, laboratory analysis results, and the following pulmonary function parameters: the forced expiratory volume in one second percentage of predicted (FEV1 %pred), forced vital capacity percentage of predicted (FVC %pred), diffusing capacity divided by the alveolar volume (DLCO/VA), DLCO, DLCO %pred. All-cause mortality data were collected throughout the 18 months follow-up period.ResultsA total of 510 IPF patients recruited for the final analysis, 131 (25.7%) died during follow-up. IPF patients who died were older, had a higher white blood cell, lactic dehydrogenase, fibrinogen and ESR. In addition, IPF patients who died had a worse pulmonary function, as evidenced by lower FEV1 %pred, FVC %pred, DLCO %pred and DLCO/VA (P<0.05). Logistic regression analysis showed that ESR was an independent risk factor for IPF patients who died, with OR=1.024, 95% CI=1.002-1.048 (P<0.05). Based on the receiver operating characteristic curve, ESR could predict all-cause mortality in IPF patients, with an area under the curve of 0.645 and a 95% CI of 0.591-0.700 (P<0.05). The optimal ESR cut-off value was determined to be 21.5 mm/h. Cox regression analysis revealed that IPF patients with an ESR ≥ 21.5 mm/h had a significantly higher all-cause mortality risk, with a hazard ratio of 5.406 and a 95% CI of 1.177-24.825 (P<0.05).ConclusionESR is a promising biomarker for predicting all-cause mortality in IPF patients.

papers.abstract_en: Alveolar repair and regeneration are critical for resolving lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI); however, the molecular mechanisms that restrain this process remain unclear. Here, we identify PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) as a critical regulator of alveolar regeneration via Hippo-YAP signaling in LIRI. Wild-type and Pink1-/- mice, as well as mice with adeno-associated virus type 6-mediated alveolar epithelium-specific knockdown or overexpression of PINK1, were subjected to left lung ischemia-reperfusion. In vitro, murine alveolar epithelial MLE-12 cells were exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/recovery (OGD/R) with PINK1 modulated genetically. We demonstrated that PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced, while PINK1 overexpression attenuated, type II alveolar epithelial cell (AT2) proliferation, nuclear translocation of YAP, and the expression of YAP target genes in LIRI. Pharmacologic inhibition of YAP abrogated, whereas YAP activation potentiated, the pro-regenerative phenotype induced by OGD/R under PINK1 knockdown. Mechanistically, PINK1 directly phosphorylated YAP at Ser127, promoting YAP cytoplasmic retention and stabilization. PINK1 deficiency reduced YAP phosphorylation, leading to increased nuclear translocation of YAP and enhanced regenerative signaling. Meanwhile, PINK1 deficiency induced alveolar basement membrane thickening and lung function decline. Collectively, our findings reveal PINK1 as a kinase-dependent brake on YAP-driven alveolar regeneration. However, PINK1 deficiency facilitates alveolar repair while simultaneously precipitating maladaptive remodeling and functional deterioration in murine LIRI, suggesting that balanced regulation of the PINK1-YAP pathway is essential during LIRI repair.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Legionnaires' disease (LD) is a severe pneumonia increasingly linked to building water systems. Although Legionella colonizes both hot- and cold-water networks, the precise source of infection often remains unclear, and the interpretation of minor genomic differences between related isolates is not well established. We aimed to assess patterns of genetic variation between sample points within water systems and evaluate whether they are consistent among the most likely sources of infection using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed LD cases in Finland from 2017 to 2024 with available WGS data from both patient and epidemiologically linked environmental isolates. Genetic relatedness was assessed using cgMLST (≤ 4 allele differences defining close relatedness). Sequence types, clustering patterns and allele differences were compared across sampling points and water system types. RESULTS: WGS of 22 clinical and 65 epidemiologically associated environmental isolates identified 14 sequence types (STs) and cgMLST grouped isolates accordingly. Isolates were genetically diverse between cases and showed no clustering beyond known outbreak-related strains, except in a single case. 73% were caused by Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1 and 23% by other L. pneumophila serogroups. Clinical and environmental isolates were closely related in 28/30 cases (93%), and at least one environmental isolate was cgMLST-identical to the patient isolate in 25 cases (83%) supporting genetic link between clinical and environmental sources. Minor allelic differences (typically 1-2 alleles) were observed in 60% of cases, with identical and closely related variants often co-occurring within the same water system. In addition, hot-water isolates were significantly more likely to match patient isolates than cold-water isolates (85% vs 44%, p = 0.001), although matching strains were also frequently detected in cold-water systems. CONCLUSIONS: WGS demonstrated high concordance between clinical and epidemiologically associated environmental isolates and supports source attribution in most LD investigations. Minor allelic differences between related isolates were common and reflected limited within-system microdiversity rather than conflicting evidence of source attribution. Integrating genomic and epidemiological data is essential for accurate interpretation of LD investigations. Hot-water isolates were more frequently identical to patient strains than cold-water isolates, although both water systems may harbor infection-associated populations.

papers.abstract_en: Early detection of esophageal cancer through non-invasive barium meal imaging is critical for improving patient outcomes, yet the weak lesion boundaries, subtle textures, and high background noise in these images pose fundamental challenges for automated detection. Current methods face two technical bottlenecks: backbone networks lose fragile edge information during downsampling, while feature pyramids introduce detail loss and spatial misalignment during upsampling, together causing high miss rates for superficial lesions and imprecise boundary localization. Here, we present EWE-DETR, a detection framework that addresses these limitations through two complementary innovations. First, an Edge-Aware Partial-Attention backbone (EAP) employs parallel edge and semantic branches to simultaneously capture local boundary details and global anatomical context, preserving lesion edges from the earliest layers. Second, a Wavelet-Enhanced Edge-Semantic Feature Pyramid Network (WES-FPN) uses wavelet transforms for frequency-preserving upsampling and cross-layer edge injection to eliminate traditional upsampling artifacts. Across 10 matched random seeds on the EC-BSID dataset, EWE-DETR achieved an mAP50 of 86.06% ± 0.19% and an F1 score of 83.20% ± 0.60%. Compared with JS-DETR, the closest-performing comparator in terms of mAP50, EWE-DETR yielded higher point estimates across all core detection metrics, including a 7.04-percentage-point improvement in precision. These findings support further evaluation of EWE-DETR as a candidate computer-aided screening tool; however, given the single-center retrospective design of this study, they do not establish its direct deployability in primary-care hospitals or across different imaging devices.

papers.abstract_en: Pressurised metered-dose inhalers (pMDIs) are a common device type used to deliver various inhaled medicines to the lungs of patients with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and other respiratory diseases. Most pMDIs use hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) propellants, such as hydrofluoroalkane (HFA)-134a, which is a powerful greenhouse gas with a 100-year global warming potential (GWP) 1530 times more potent than CO2. Legislation in developed countries, particularly in Europe, will reduce the availability of high-GWP propellants, enforcing the phase-down of HFC-containing pMDIs within the next five years. Inhaler manufacturers are at various stages of research and development and regulatory approval to reformulate pMDIs with next-generation propellants (HFA-152a, hydrofluoroolefin (HFO)-1234ze[E]) with a much lower carbon footprint. If the transition is not carefully managed, there are risks to patient health. From the patient perspective, the transition must be seamless. Here we aim to provide a clear, consensus-based framework to deliver this transition. Following a policy roundtable which included stakeholders across the respiratory community, four key principles were outlined: (1) patient safety and seamless continuity of access; (2) securing supply through shared responsibility and collaboration across the respiratory community; (3) alignment of regulatory and policy interventions across jurisdictions; (4) building trust through credible, clinician-centred communication. These principles prioritise patient health, while recognising the need to balance environmental commitments as we transition from current to low-GWP inhalers. This framework serves as a call to action, and we encourage all respiratory stakeholders to use the principles as a foundation for external discussions with policymakers and regulators.

papers.abstract_en: Chest X-ray report generation aims to produce diagnostic descriptions grounded in imaging evidence. However, correlation-driven models may exploit reporting templates and disease co-occurrence patterns, leading to unsupported findings and semantic drift. To address this issue, we propose C3E-RRG, a confounder-aware causal debiasing framework for chest X-ray report generation that incorporates explicit causal modeling into the encoder-decoder pipeline. Specifically, we first construct confounding variables by combining language priors derived from pointwise mutual information with disease co-occurrence statistics, and apply confounder-aware adjustment to suppress spurious correlations induced by data bias. We then design an evidence-consistent cross-modal coupling module to strengthen the correspondence between visual features and diagnostic semantics, thereby reducing semantic drift caused by high-frequency reporting templates. Finally, we develop a dynamic bidirectional causal evolution mechanism that iteratively revisits visual evidence and refines semantic representations, progressively correcting semantic deviations and improving image-text consistency during long-sequence generation. Experiments on the IU-XRay and MIMIC-CXR datasets demonstrate competitive performance and validate the effectiveness of the proposed components in suppressing confounding effects, aligning visual evidence with diagnostic semantics, and dynamically correcting generation errors. The source code is available at https://github.com/ cloneiq/C3E-RRG.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) causes inflammatory alveolar-capillary injury at different ages. Age-related differences in respiratory mechanics, airway anatomy, pulmonary vascular physiology, and disease etiology limit extrapolation of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. This review compared respiratory monitoring and support strategies across adult, pediatric, and neonatal ARDS. AREAS COVERED: We searched PubMed for English-language human studies published from database inception through 14 August 2026 and reviewed major society guidelines. This review covers age-specific ARDS definitions, epidemiology, pathophysiology, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and liberation from mechanical ventilation. Adult-derived evidence supports low-tidal-volume ventilation, prolonged prone positioning for severe ARDS, selective higher positive end-expiratory pressure, and early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for refractory disease. Recommendations for pediatric ARDS often rely on consensus or observational evidence. Neonatal ARDS management remains largely extrapolated from neonatal respiratory disorders and must account for gestational age, surfactant biology, pulmonary hypertension, and etiology. EXPERT OPINION: Respiratory support should be age-calibrated, phenotype-informed, and reassessed for gas exchange, respiratory effort, mechanics, hemodynamics, device performance, and clinical trajectory. Physiological improvements may not translate into positive outcomes. Noninvasive support should not delay intubation in cases of failure. Standardized interventions and prospective studies must be tailored to pediatric and neonatal populations.

papers.abstract_en: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Pathological respiratory chemoreflex activation (high loop gain) in sleep apnea may activate the carotid body and induce excessive sympathetic nerve output, and independently add to the risk of adverse outcomes. This study aims to determine whether a high loop gain of the respiratory control system during sleep, estimated by respiratory self-similarity (SS) and the algorithm-derived central respiratory event index (CREI), is associated with new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and CVD-related mortality. METHODS: A secondary analysis of The Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) and Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA). High SS% and CREI were defined as the highest quartile. Lasso regression and restricted cubic spline assessed the relationship between SS%, CREI and CVD, CVD-mortality and all-cause mortality. A cumulative incidence function and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model were used to evaluate this outcome accounting for competing risks. RESULTS: In adjusted models with age as a categorical variable divided by 65 years old, the highest quartile of SS% (HR 1.693, p: 0.017 in MESA and HR 1.240, p : 0.009 in SHHS) was associated with the incidence of CVD and was more prominent in males. A positive relationship between SS% (MESA: HR 1.429, p: 0.039; SHHS HR1.176, p:0.018 ) for the continuous metrics and CVD mortality in both cohorts was more apparent in men than in women. The categorical high-exposure association with CVD mortality was not consistent across cohorts.The associations were significantly attenuated when adjusted by age as a continuous metric. CONCLUSIONS: An endotype of sleep apnea reflecting high loop gain is associated with CVD and CVD mortality, especially in males.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: National-scale evidence linking flooding to legionellosis relies heavily on aggregated surveillance time series, which are vulnerable to data-extraction error and seasonal confounding. An earlier version of this study reported a positive flood-legionellosis association in U.S. surveillance data; during revision we discovered errors in our data-extraction pipeline. This article corrects the record in full. OBJECTIVES: To present a corrected, transparently audited reanalysis and to quantify how extraction errors and shared seasonality can generate spurious flood-health associations. METHODS: We re-parsed all 299 CDC NNDSS weekly tables (2019-2024) using a coordinate-anchored parser reconciled week-by-week against the printed U.S. totals (299/299 weeks reconciled exactly). Flood exposures came from the NOAA Storm Events Database. Fixed-effects Poisson and negative-binomial distributed-lag models included state and year-week fixed effects, state-specific linear trends, state-specific Fourier seasonality, and temperature terms, with permutation and event-study diagnostics. RESULTS: The corrected panel comprises 15,197 state-weeks and 11,676 legionellosis cases. The originally submitted association (average lag-0-5 IRR 1.11, 95% CI 1.06-1.17) arose from inflated 2023 counts caused by column misreads (weekly national totals of roughly 300-400 versus 15-46 after correction) acting together with seasonal confounding. On the corrected data the headline association is null (IRR 1.015, 95% CI 0.981-1.051; p = 0.39; permutation p = 0.58; event-study post-event coefficients all null). DISCUSSION: The flood-legionellosis association in our earlier submission was an artefact. Surveillance-based flood-health studies should reconcile extracted series against printed totals and treat flexible seasonal adjustment as mandatory.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to objectively evaluate the presence of allergic reactions and pulmonary function in individuals working in small container-like confined spaces in Malatya following the February 6, 2023, Kahramanmaraş-centered earthquakes, and to examine their associations with physical activity, sleep quality, grip strength, and quality of life. Given the well-established association between respiratory impairment and systemic effects on peripheral muscle strength, sleep architecture, and functional capacity, grip strength, sleep quality (PSQI), and physical activity (IPAQ-SF) were included as secondary outcomes to capture the broader functional burden of working in confined environments. METHODS: This cross-sectional and descriptive study included 90 volunteers (aged 25-55 years) working in container-like spaces for at least two years. Pulmonary function was assessed using portable spirometry (FEV₁, FVC, FEV₁/FVC) according to the 2019 ATS/ERS guidelines, performed by trained physiotherapists. Physical activity was evaluated with IPAQ-SF, sleep quality with PSQI, quality of life with SF-36, and grip strength with a digital dynamometer. Multiple linear regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of respiratory function, controlling for age, smoking status, BMI, height, grip strength, and fatigue. RESULTS: Of 90 participants (92.2% male, mean age 39.0 ± 9.5 years), FEV₁% (68.9 ± 12.4) and FVC% (64.1 ± 11.3) were relatively low with a preserved FEV₁/FVC ratio (0.86 ± 0.06). mMRC dyspnea grade was significantly associated with FEV₁% and FVC% (p < 0.001). Multiple linear regression revealed that fatigue was a significant independent predictor of FEV₁% (β=-0.945, p = 0.044) and FEV₁ (L) (β=-0.053, p = 0.029) after controlling for confounders. Grip strength showed a positive trend with FEV₁% (β = 0.282, p = 0.082) and FVC% (β = 0.242, p = 0.092) that approached significance, consistent with the physiological link between respiratory and peripheral muscle function. The overall regression models were statistically significant (p < 0.01 for all models). CONCLUSION: Individuals working in small container-like spaces showed a tendency toward reduced ventilatory capacity without overt obstruction, and dyspnea was strongly associated with objective respiratory function loss. Fatigue emerged as an independent predictor of respiratory function. These findings highlight the importance of early screening strategies and further research with longitudinal designs, environmental measurements, and control groups to establish causal relationships.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for about 85% of all cases. Current emerging treatment options still show limited clinical benefit, making chemotherapy an important part of NSCLC management. Although multiple clinical trials have demonstrated the efficacy of carboplatin combined with paclitaxel in patients with NSCLC, adverse reactions and safety concerns associated with traditional chemotherapy administration remain significant, highlighting the need for alternative drug delivery strategies. Pulmonary drug delivery enables direct drug deposition in the lungs with reduced systemic exposure. Dry powder formulations provide an alternative to liquid aerosol systems for pulmonary drug delivery, with electrospraying offering a flexible approach for preparing inhalable dry powder particles. In this study, electrosprayed particles based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and chitosan were developed and optimised for the pulmonary delivery of paclitaxel and carboplatin. The particles were characterised using electron microscopy, laser diffraction, and next-generation impactor, and their biological performance was evaluated in A549 and Calu-3 cells. Despite a primary particle size below 1 μm, particle aggregation led to volumetric and aerodynamic diameters within the optimal range (1-5 μm) for pulmonary deposition. The formulations showed low moisture content (<3% w/w) with good aerosol performance, achieving over 80% emitted dose and the highest effective fine particle fraction of 58.61 ± 0.83%. Both drugs were successfully encapsulated with a rapid release of 70-90% within the first 2 h. Chitosan coating increased particle adhesion and cell interaction, and cell viability studies confirmed cytotoxic effects against A549 cells over 72 h.

papers.abstract_en: The protective adaptation of innate immune defenses against respiratory pathogens has been linked to previous exposure to immune stimuli; however, the underlying mechanisms of these adaptations are not yet fully understood. Here, we show that pre-exposure to a low dose of non-specific immune stimuli or infection protects against subsequent lethal methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) challenge. This enhanced protection concurs with increased alveolar macrophages (AMs) resulting from a self-renewal process in the lungs. Importantly, these AMs are programmed to acquire neutrophil-released antimicrobial enzymes from the extracellular space to clear MRSA, prevent tissue damage, and rapidly restore lung homeostasis. AM function depends on differential gene expression, including expression of the efferocytosis receptor Mer proto-oncogene tyrosine kinase (MerTK) and the anti-apoptotic regulator Bcl-xL. Thus, our data highlight that AMs acquire neutrophil enzymes as an integral component of innate immune adaptation.

papers.title_zh: 巴基斯坦COVID-19前后流感流行病学变化的10年FluNet分析：B型比例持续升高、A(H1N1)pdm09恢复主导但H3仍高于疫情前
papers.title_en: Temporal Shifting of Influenza Subtype Dynamics in Pakistan Following the COVID-19 Pandemic: A 10-Year FluNet Analysis, 2015-2024.
papers.authors: Qureshi AJ, Tagga MRT, Ali H, Tariq A, Yattassaye M
papers.affiliation_highlight: CMH Multan Institute of Medical Sciences, Multan, Pakistan.
papers.results: 流感A占比由94.2%降至71.7%后回升至77.5%；流感B由5.7%升至28.3%后为22.5%（p < 0.001）。A(H3)在疫情干扰期占主导（98.8%）；A(H1N1)pdm09在疫情后恢复主导（58.8%），而A(H3)仍高于疫情前（41.2% vs 33.3%）。峰值强度差异有统计学意义（p = 0.047）：疫情前33.3%-67.6%，疫情干扰期14.0%-17.6%，疫情后19.8%-37.8%。流行季时长：2020年1周、2021年3个不连续周，疫情前为10-16周，疫情后恢复至7-13周。
papers.authors_conclusion: COVID-19疫情造成了巴基斯坦流感流行病学的持久改变，流感B持续升高、A亚型平衡被重塑；这些发现与全球B/Yamagata消失相一致，支持考虑三价疫苗配方，但仍需抗原和遗传数据确认疫苗匹配性。
papers.ai_note: 各阶段检测量极不均衡（10,781 vs 14,687 vs 54,016），且疫情期间检测行为、上报完整性与FluNet覆盖机构可能变化，单纯构成比（百分比）比较易受检测与报告偏倚影响，摘要未见对检测量或机构数的标准化/校正；流行季时长以阳性率≥10%为阈值，该阈值在低流行期会放大缩短效应；生态学时间序列无法将变化归因于NPIs本身；作者由血清型构成推断支持三价疫苗，但承认缺乏抗原/遗传数据（B/Yamagata消失为间接推断，无本研究的毒株谱系数据）；无疫苗有效性或抗原匹配的直接终点，结论与证据链之间存在信息不足。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated nonpharmaceutical interventions caused unprecedented suppression of influenza circulation globally. Pakistan, with its high population density and evolving surveillance capacity, lacks long-term data on post-COVID-19 influenza patterns, essential for guiding vaccine policy. METHODS: We extracted weekly virological data for Pakistan from the WHO FluNet platform (January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024). The study period was divided into pre-COVID-19 (2015-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 (2022-2024) phases. Outcomes included type A versus B proportion, subtype distribution (A[H1N1]pdm09 vs. A[H3]), positivity, peak intensity, and season duration (weeks with positivity ≥ 10%). Statistical comparisons used chi-square for subtype distribution and Kruskal-Wallis for peak intensity. RESULTS: We analyzed 6522 positive specimens from 79,484 tested (10,781 pre-COVID-19; 14,687 during COVID-19 disruption; 54,016 post-COVID-19). Influenza A declined from 94.2% to 71.7% then rose to 77.5%; influenza B increased from 5.7% to 28.3%, remaining at 22.5% (p < 0.001). A(H3) dominated during the COVID-19 disruption (98.8%); A(H1N1)pdm09 regained dominance post-COVID-19 (58.8%), though A(H3) remained higher than pre-COVID-19 (41.2% vs. 33.3%). Peak intensity differed (p = 0.047): pre-COVID-19 33.3%-67.6%; COVID-19 disruption 14.0%-17.6%; and post-COVID-19 19.8%-37.8%. Season duration was 1 week in 2020 and 3 non-consecutive weeks in 2021, versus 10-16 weeks pre-COVID-19, recovering to 7-13 weeks post-COVID-19. CONCLUSION: The COVID-19 pandemic induced a lasting shift in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, with persistently elevated influenza B and reshaped A subtype balance. These findings are consistent with the global disappearance of B/Yamagata and support consideration of trivalent vaccine formulations, though antigenic and genetic data remain necessary to confirm vaccine match.
